sections.purpose: To measure optical density (OD) of microbial cultures and absorbance of coloured solutions for growth curve analysis, cell count estimation, and colorimetric assays in the Microbiology laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Microbiology laboratory for turbidity measurements (OD₆₀₀), enzyme assay absorbance readings, and colorimetric test analysis.
procedure: Switch on the spectrophotometer and allow it to warm up for a minimum of 15–20 minutes before use.
Set the required wavelength using the wavelength selector: OD₆₀₀ for bacterial growth; specific wavelengths for colorimetric assays.
Select the appropriate measurement mode: Absorbance (A) for most microbiology measurements.
Clean a pair of matched cuvettes thoroughly and rinse with the blank solution (uninoculated broth or buffer).
Fill the reference cuvette with the blank solution and wipe the exterior with lens paper.
Insert the reference (blank) cuvette into the reference beam holder and press 'Zero' or 'Blank' to set the baseline.
Prepare the sample: For turbidity, pipette the microbial suspension directly; dilute if OD exceeds 1.0.
Fill the sample cuvette with the bacterial suspension or test solution, wipe the exterior, and insert into the sample holder.
Close the sample compartment lid and record the absorbance value displayed.
For growth curves: measure OD at regular time intervals; correlate OD values with cell counts using a pre-established calibration curve.
After measurements, remove cuvettes, rinse with distilled water and dry or store in appropriate solvent.
Record all wavelengths, readings, dilution factors, and sample details in the laboratory register.
Switch off the instrument after use and cover it with the dust cover.
precautions: Allow adequate warm-up time before measurements — readings taken before stabilization are inaccurate.
Use the correct type of cuvette: Quartz cuvettes for UV range (below 340 nm); glass or plastic for visible range (340–900 nm).
Always blank the instrument with the appropriate reference solution before sample measurements.
Keep OD readings in the linear range (0.1–0.8 AU) for accurate Beer-Lambert law compliance — dilute if above this range.
Wipe cuvette exterior with lens tissue only — rough tissues scratch optical surfaces.
Do not allow microbial suspensions to sit in cuvettes for extended periods — this causes biofilm formation.
Decontaminate all cuvettes and pipette tips used with microbial cultures before washing.
Check wavelength accuracy periodically using standard reference solutions.
Keep the sample compartment free of dust and liquid spills — clean immediately if spillage occurs.
